chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from a man from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu al-Jarud from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'The Muslims exerted themselves greatly in Khaybar, and the Muslims hastened with their beasts of burden, so the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered the covering of the cooking pots, and did not say that they were forbidden, and that was to preserve the beasts of burden.'

key_terms.أَجْهَدُوا: They exerted themselves greatly / worked hard.
key_terms.إِبْقَاءً عَلَى الدَّوَابِّ: Preservation of the beasts of burden.
key_terms.خَيْبَرَ: Khaybar, a historical location and site of a major military expedition.
key_terms.دَوَابِّهِمْ: Their beasts of burden (animals used for carrying loads).

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet order the cooking pots to be covered during the expedition to Khaybar?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrates that during the expedition to Khaybar, the Muslims exerted great effort and hurried their beasts of burden. To prevent the animals from tiring, the Prophet ordered the cooking pots to be covered (to keep food warm without constant stirring or attention), clarifying that this act was not a prohibition (haram) but a practical measure for preservation.
